clue.text: Unfortunately, Brit's need to admit crime is a sign of lacking legitimacy

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one piece is taken inside the other
things that go unfortunately go wrong, so these letters end up in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A British person sadly needs to confess wrongdoing, which marks them as illegitimate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a sign of lacking legitimacy' is heraldic: the crime goes into the middle of the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry a diagonal band running from upper right to lower left on a shield traditionally marked a bastard line.

clue.text: Supports faction's pre-strike motion

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
a wing is a faction within a party

explanation.surface: A political group endorses a motion ahead of a planned industrial strike.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all trade-union politics; the strike is actually the hit of a club or bat.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf or cricket the backswing is the movement drawing the club or bat back before hitting the ball.

clue.text: Complex football tournament, one held by the Poles

indicators.note: something held by another is gripped on both sides, so it sits within

parts.note: north and south, the two poles

explanation.surface: A European football championship with one competitor hosted by Poland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Poles' looks like the people of Poland, but it means the North and South poles.
explanation.definitionFit: A complex in the psychological sense is an obsessive anxiety or fixation, much like a neurotic disorder.

clue.text: A part cut by Head of Music Department

indicators.note: a word cut by another is split open with something lodged in the gap

parts.note: some is a part of the whole

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter only

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Part of a budget is trimmed by the head of a school's music department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of Music Department' reads as a job title, but Department is the definition: France is divided into départements.
explanation.definitionFit: The Somme is one of the administrative regions of northern France, named after its river.

clue.text: Architect left hideous houses in country's main city

parts.note: John Nash, architect of Regency London

indicators.note: a building houses its occupants by keeping them inside

explanation.surface: An architect abandoned ugly housing in a nation's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country's main city' looks like a national capital, but country means country music.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tennessee city is known as the capital of country music, home of the Grand Ole Opry.

clue.text: Becoming crafty, keeping tabs on Mark

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: tabs are tablets, and E is ecstasy, so two pills
M for the old German mark

explanation.surface: Someone grows cunning while watching Mark closely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping tabs on' looks like one phrase meaning to watch; split it and tabs are ecstasy pills placed on Mark, all inside the word for crafty.
explanation.definitionFit: Becoming in the sense of fitting or appropriate, as in becoming behaviour, means proper and decorous.

clue.text: Madonna's part Aboriginal, but not originally from down under

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading from the bottom upwards runs the word backwards
what is not there originally lacks its starting letter

parts.note: an aboriginal person is a native of the land

explanation.surface: The singer's role is partly Aboriginal, though not originally from Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down under' suggests Australia, chiming with Aboriginal; in this down clue it means read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Madonna played Eva Perón in the 1996 film of the Lloyd Webber musical, the title role.

clue.text: Where art lovers go, you said, racing to drink a lot of champagne

indicators.note: to drink is to take in, so one piece swallows the other
said means spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: the letter that sounds like the word
F1, Formula One motor racing, with the 1 read as I

indicators.note: a lot of something is most but not all, so the tail is dropped

parts.note: fizz is slang for sparkling wine

explanation.surface: Someone describes a party racing off to drink plenty of bubbly.
explanation.walkthrough: Racing is Formula One, written F1 with the digit read as the letter I; 'a lot of' trims the champagne word before it goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Uffizi in Florence is one of the world's great galleries of Renaissance painting, a magnet for visitors.

clue.text: Escorts family inside Poe's mansion

definitions.meaning: first meaning: shows people to their places
second meaning: the doomed household in Edgar Allan Poe's tale of a crumbling house

explanation.walkthrough: In The Fall of the House of Usher, Roderick and Madeline are the family inside the mansion.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre attendants guide guests to seats, and the surname is also that of Poe's ill-fated siblings.

clue.text: Pacific hurricane goes around cape

indicators.note: the phrase goes around the answer, wrapping it inside its own letters

explanation.surface: A Pacific storm swirls around a headland.
explanation.walkthrough: Cape looks geographical, a headland the storm passes; it is the garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A fichu is a small triangular shawl worn round the shoulders, a kind of short cape.

clue.text: Puzzles Picaroon's set taking time

indicators.note: taking something in means it ends up inside

explanation.surface: The setter's crosswords take a while to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: Picaroon is this puzzle's setter, so his name gives the possessive MY.
explanation.definitionFit: Puzzles as a noun are enigmas or things that baffle, which is what mysteries are.

clue.text: About to come home, dashed to collect son

indicators.note: collecting something means picking it up and holding it

explanation.surface: A parent heads home after rushing to pick up their son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to come' looks like wordplay (about as a container), but it is the whole definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in store is waiting in the future, imminent or lying ahead for someone.

clue.text: Hamlet's struggle to hold bitterness back

indicators.note: to hold is to keep inside, so one piece contains the other
back means going the other way, so the word runs right to left

explanation.surface: The Prince of Denmark struggles to suppress his bitter resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet looks like Shakespeare's prince, but it is a small settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamlet is a small rural settlement, usually smaller than a village but close enough to serve as a synonym.

clue.text: One small, revolving board unable to be taken off?

indicators.note: a word that revolves turns round so it faces the other way

parts.note: board can mean a table, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: A small rotating board that cannot be removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken off' sounds like removed, but it means mimicked or impersonated.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone off is to imitate them, so something impossible to copy is beyond imitation.

clue.text: Trees burning somewhere in Hampshire

explanation.surface: A forest fire somewhere in southern England.
explanation.walkthrough: Hampshire is a county on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldershot is a town in north-east Hampshire, famous as the home of the British Army.

clue.text: Cycling, go by places like Cheltenham

indicators.note: cycling moves letters round in a loop, end letter coming round to the front

parts.note: to pass is to go by

explanation.surface: Cyclists ride past English towns.
explanation.walkthrough: The final S moves round to the front. Cheltenham is an English town famous for its mineral springs.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheltenham grew as a resort around healing waters, making it a classic example of an English spa town.

clue.text: Wraps Ralph Fiennes or Judi Dench in Turkish bigwig's clothes

indicators.note: to clothe something is to cover it all round

parts.note: a pasha was a high-ranking Ottoman official
both played the spy chief M in James Bond films

explanation.surface: Two famous actors are dressed in a Turkish dignitary's outfits.
explanation.walkthrough: The actors are linked by the one-letter role they shared in the Bond films.
explanation.definitionFit: Pashminas are fine woollen shawls, worn draped round the shoulders as wraps.

clue.text: Seen tucking into breakfast roll, Eric Ambler

indicators.note: something seen tucking into food is buried in the middle of the phrase

explanation.surface: Eric Ambler, the thriller writer, is spotted eating a breakfast roll.
explanation.walkthrough: Eric Ambler was a real novelist, so the name reads as one; Ambler is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambler walks at a leisurely pace, and so does someone out for a stroll.

clue.text: One-piece garment American obtained from the east

indicators.note: in an across clue, reading from the east means right to left

explanation.surface: An American picks up a swimsuit imported from Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman toga was a single long piece of cloth wrapped round the body.

clue.text: Hem of tiny trousers long or short?

indicators.note: to trouser is to pocket, so one piece is stowed inside
the hem is the edge, so only the outside letters are kept

parts.note: to long for is to itch for

explanation.surface: A tailor wonders whether a little pair of trousers should be hemmed long or short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' is a verb here, meaning pockets. Titchy is British slang for very small.
explanation.definitionFit: Titchy is informal British slang for very small, and short people may be described with it.

clue.text: A health worker's nursing five people expecting salvation soon

indicators.note: nursing something means cradling it in one's arms

parts.note: a dentist cares for teeth, with the possessive s

explanation.surface: A medic looks after five patients hoping to be saved quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: V goes inside DENTISTS after the D.
explanation.definitionFit: Adventists are Christians who believe the second coming of Christ is imminent.

clue.text: Capital of Serbia south of Split

indicators.note: a capital letter is the one at the front, so only the opening letter counts

parts.note: on a map, south of means beneath

explanation.surface: Belgrade lies south of the Croatian city of Split.
explanation.walkthrough: Split looks like the Croatian port, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To sunder is a literary word for dividing or breaking apart, which means to split.

clue.text: Very involved with small-label record one put out

indicators.note: putting something out removes it from where it was

parts.note: an indie is an independent record label

explanation.surface: A small independent label puts out a record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' looks like releasing the record, but it means removing one I from INDIE.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in deep is to be heavily committed or entangled in something, often trouble.

clue.text: On public transport, I'm not sure one goes on foot

parts.note: a train is a form of public transport
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A rail passenger wonders whether walking would be better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one goes on foot' sounds like a walker, but the definition means something worn on a foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainer is a sports shoe, so it is an item worn on the foot.

clue.text: People not drinking Riesling drained last of vermouth that's horrible

indicators.note: a drained container has nothing inside, leaving only its outer letters
the last of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Teetotallers drink up the wine and find the vermouth dreadful.
explanation.definitionFit: Aargh is a cry of disgust or frustration, an exclamation meaning roughly how awful.

clue.text: Theatrical assistant's article on supporting Starmer

parts.note: Keir Starmer, the UK Prime Minister

explanation.surface: A stagehand writes an article backing the Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' puts AN after the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A propman looks after stage properties, the objects actors handle during a production.

clue.text: Tree bearing fruit twice a year? Wife sits beneath it

explanation.surface: A wife sits under a tree that fruits twice yearly.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, a letter that sits beneath the rest comes after it. The abbreviation for per annum is doubled.
explanation.definitionFit: The papaw or pawpaw is a tree grown for its edible fruit, the papaya.

clue.text: Inducement to speed or another drug with joint

explanation.surface: A list of drugs: speed, or another one, together with a joint.
explanation.walkthrough: Speed looks like the amphetamine, which makes 'or another drug' natural; but speed is going fast.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider lashes a mount with this to make it go faster, so it is an incentive to hurry.

clue.text: Lover of Kent tours Canterbury at first, getting puncture

indicators.note: to tour a place is to go all round it

parts.note: Lois Lane loves Clark Kent in Superman

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter alone

explanation.surface: A sweetheart from the county of Kent visits Canterbury and gets a flat tyre.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent looks like the English county, where Canterbury is; it is Clark Kent, Superman.
explanation.definitionFit: To lance a boil is to pierce it, so the verb means to puncture.

clue.text: He stops twisting issue raised by Guardian for Labour representatives

indicators.note: twisting something bends it out of its shape, so these letters get rearranged

parts.note: issue means children, and those brought up by a guardian are wards

explanation.surface: A union man halts the Guardian newspaper's spin on a story.
explanation.walkthrough: The Guardian is the newspaper running this puzzle; 'issue raised' sounds like a matter brought up, but issue is offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: Shop stewards are elected union officials representing workers, Labour in the sense of the workforce.
